items.sentence: Software and services revenue rose 221.7% to $1,557 million, 28.9% of revenue, on vehicle electrical architecture and software development services for the Joint Venture plus remarketing and repair .

items.sentence: Automotive revenue fell 14.6% as deliveries dropped 9,332 vehicles, partly from expiration of 45W tax credits after September 30, 2025 .

passages.filing: FY2025 10-K Item 7. Management's Discussion and Analysis
passages.text: Automotive revenues decreased for the year ended December 31, 2025, primarily resulting from a decrease in deliveries of 9,332 vehicles, due in part to the expiration of 45W tax credits after September 30, 2025, as well as a decrease in sales of automotive regulatory credits, partially offset by higher average selling prices and a higher mix of R1 deliveries. The increase in average selling prices was driven by a consumer shift towards higher performance variants along with a decline in discounting.

items.label: supported
items.reason: P22 cites a 9,332-vehicle delivery decline, partly due to 45W credit expiration after September 30, 2025.

items.sentence: Cost of revenue fell 15.0% and drove 26.8pp of the margin bridge, as fewer vehicles were produced and raw material and conversion costs fell .

passages.filing: FY2025 10-K Item 7. Management's Discussion and Analysis
passages.text: For the year ended December 31, 2025, Automotive cost of revenues included $484 million of depreciation and amortization expense and $43 million of stock-based compensation expense. The year-over-year decrease in Automotive cost of revenues was primarily due to fewer vehicles being produced and delivered, as well as reductions in the cost of raw materials, product components, and conversion costs, resulting in part from the cost of revenue efficiency initiatives and accelerated depreciation that occurred during the prior year.

items.label: partial
items.reason: P21 gives these causes for Automotive cost of revenues, not for total cost of revenue.

items.sentence: SG&A subtracted 0.5pp as go-to-market expansion raised payroll and stock-based compensation .

passages.filing: FY2025 10-K Item 7. Management's Discussion and Analysis
passages.text: For the year ended December 31, 2025, SG&A expenses included $221 million of depreciation and amortization expense and $324 million of stock-based compensation expense. SG&A expenses increased as a result of expanding our go-to-market operations and footprint, including higher payroll and related expenses primarily driven by increased headcount, stock-based compensation expenses primarily attributable to an increase in the total amount of accrued stock-based bonus incentives, and facilities expenses.

items.label: supported
items.reason: P13 attributes the SG&A increase to go-to-market expansion, higher payroll and stock-based compensation.

passages.text: Other expense, net increased for the year ended December 31, 2025 primarily due to $186 million of expense recorded for the settlement of securities class action litigation, net of expected insurance recoveries, which was partially offset by the cumulative gain on our equity method investment in Also, Inc. items.sentence: Financing inflow of $886 million came mainly from $750 million of Class A shares issued to Volkswagen Group, and diluted shares rose 17.1% .

passages.text: Net cash provided by financing activities during the year ended December 31, 2025 primarily resulted from the issuance of $750 million in shares of Class A common stock to Volkswagen Group in connection with the achievement of the Financial Milestone, as well as capital contributed by outside parties in the formation of Mind Robotics, Inc. and Mind Robotics, LLC (see Note 1 "Presentation and Nature of Operations" and Note 19 “Variable Interest Entities” to our consolidated financial statements included in this Form 10-K for more information).
